title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, 50, of Tennessee is suing Fargo, North Dakota and police detective Lucas Heck for $10m after being falsely arrested and jailed for about six months. US marshals took her at gunpoint from her home in July 2025 while she was babysitting four children. She spent nearly four months in a Tennessee jail awaiting extradition and about two more months in North Dakota on theft and identity fraud charges. The charges were dropped after her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee at the time of the Fargo fraud.

Her lawsuit says Fargo police relied on an AI facial recognition match from a fake ID and surveillance video, even though Lipps did not resemble the suspect and had never been to North Dakota. It alleges detective Heck sought an arrest warrant without enough probable cause and that the department lacked proper training and oversight. Lipps lost her home, car, and belongings, and was denied medications and dentures in custody. The city declined to comment on pending litigation, and Lipps is seeking accountability through the federal suit.
